Issued at 329 AM EDT Fri May 15 2026

Early this morning RAP analysis and GOES water vapor imagery showed 
a decaying ridge over the Upper Great lakes ahead of an upper level 
low moving through Manitoba. Southerly flow was bringing Gulf 
moisture north into the region, though sfc moisture was rather 
meager. Elevated moisture combined with waa was producing a band of 
showers, currently over the western U.P. tracking eastwards. It was 
a mild night with temperatures in the low 50s to low 60s over the 
central and west, cooler 30s in the east where the winds were light 
and the boundary layer was able to decouple. Temperatures will 
likely warm a bit in the east over the next few hours as clouds move 
overhead.

Showers will continue to push east, exiting the eastern U.P. around 
mid-morning. Behind the showers skies will clear with mainly sunny 
skies this afternoon. As temperatures warm this morning southwest 
winds will become gusty as a mixed layer reaches into a 40kt LLJ. As 
mixing continues to increase the LLJ will decay but deeper mixing 
all the way up to 500mb will continue to bring gusty winds, 
especially late this afternoon over the west as winds in the 700-
500mb layer increase to 40-60kt. Expect winds gusts to 35 mph for 
the north-central and west, with somewhat lighter winds over the 
south-central. Winds will also remain stronger in the east from the 
south with a tighter sfc pressure gradient in place. Temperatures 
will rise into the 70s to low 80s over the central and west with 60s 
over the east where flow off of Lake Michigan will modify (cool) the 
low level airmass. The biggest concern today will be elevated to 
critical fire weather conditions over the western and central U.P, a 
big focus of the grid edits were on dew points for today. The latest 
NBM has become more moist in the low levels, maintaining dewpoints 
in the 40s over all of the U.P. through the afternoon. Bufr 
soundings support much drier conditions though, with mixing bringing 
dew points down into the mid 30s, or possibly lower. Opted to go 
with lower dew points and thus humidity, which falls into the 20-30% 
range this afternoon central/west. The combination of gusty winds 
and low humidity will bring critical fire weather conditions to the 
west and elevated fire weather conditions over much of the central 
U.P. Will maintain the red flag warning and introduce an SPS for 
areas with elevated fire weather conditions.

Medium range guidance and CAMs have homed in on isolated to 
scattered elevated showers and thunderstorms developing over the 
central and east by early evening as a weak cold front pushes 
through the area, with MUCAPE of 500-750 J/kg ahead of the front.
The combination of ample dry air, with classic inverted-v 
thermodynamic profiles and strong winds in the mid-levels will bring 
the threat for gusty and erratic winds with any showers or 
thunderstorms that develop over the central U.P. This will be 
especially true during the early evening hours when the low levels 
will remain well mixed.

It will be another mild night tonight, with lows in the 50s west and 
40s east. Humidity recoveries will be poor tonight over the west, 50-
60% range.

Flow overhead becomes zonal on Saturday with an elongated mid level 
wave grazing the northern end of the CWA. Limited moisture and 
forcing mean dry weather likely persists (90% chance). Breezy west 
winds start the day off, gusting into the 20-25 mph range, but taper 
off in the afternoon as the gradient flow weakens and weak ridging 
begins building in from the Canadian Prairie. Highs will be in the 
60s to low 80s, warmest south. Once again efficient mixing from dry 
air aloft presents another SPS day for elevated fire weather 
conditions. This high pressure influence persists through much of 
Sunday. Saturday night will be cooler in the upper 30s to 40s, 
warming up on Sunday into the upper 50s to low 70s; interior west 
reaches into the mid 70s. Sunday presents the last day for possibly 
elevated fire weather conditions interior west as winds pick up in 
the afternoon when RHs dip toward 30% or slightly lower. This will 
depend on how quick cloud cover ahead of the next precip arrives.

Attention then turns to a trough over the Rockies that sends 
shortwaves and possibly multiple surface lows over the region Sunday 
night through Tuesday. While model agreement in the pattern has 
improved somewhat in the last 24 hours, noteworthy changes in the 
overall narrative have occurred and still could given that this 
energy is still out over the Pacific...so confidence in exact 
details or timing is low. Overall expecting multiple rounds of 
showers and storms Sunday night through Tuesday. A warm airmass with 
a good Gulf connection ahead of these waves primes the region with 
ample moisture (PWATs between 1.25 and 1.75 inches) and instability. 
A warm front and primary shortwave likely bring the first wave
